segments.t: All right, to help me break down all this market action,
let's bring in my first guest.
That's going to be Joe Mazzola,
head trading and derivative strategist at Charles Schwab.
Joe, I wanted to get your take here.
We've had a couple days of weakness led by tech.
Now, I noticed yesterday, out of the 11 S&P 500 sectors,
only eight of them were positive, only three were negative.
But when you have communication services, information technology,
negative, it's getting reflected here again today.
So this tech sell-off, kind of grabbing a hold of the market at this point.
Yeah, I think you can make the case that Google probably drove a lot of those
communication services losses.
And I would even go as far as to say,
some of the funding that we've seen kind of come out of the tech sector,
whereas they've been going to the debt markets,
it's really changed the dynamic of some of these companies.
Now, to be honest, look, they're still very much cash rich.
But these were companies that for four or five years,
we were looking to as almost havens in terms of kind of their cash holdings.
And now that they've gone to start maybe finance or debt markets,
seeing more and more additional liquidity from going to the equity markets
and even issuing new shares with some of these companies,
it's changing the dynamic a little bit for some of the weighted average cost
of capital for some of these companies.
And now, yeah, it's understandable that markets are reacting a little bit,
maybe to some of the froth that's built into them.
Yeah, and you know, you take into account the fact that,
hey, the earnings have been driving the markets this year, right?
We're still just below record highs, as I mentioned,
small caps hit a record high yesterday.
But the part of the problem I'm seeing now is that these valuations,
based on earnings, starting to come in a little bit
on some of these companies.
I mean, you looked at the moves yesterday.
You mentioned Google Alphabet was down over 5%.
Amazon got hit yesterday.
Microsoft's at levels we haven't seen for nearly a year
or something like that.
And you're seeing meta platforms.
